correctness.rationale: Writing A=g^a, B=g^b makes A^k/B^t either 1 or at distance at least 1/2 from 1. The digit equation bounds its discrepancy times A^m by 2C+1, proving uniform eventual resonance, even with unbounded t,k. The remaining condition is precisely Euclidean division with quotient c_m (also for negative offsets). Positive offsets at least double; for offsets below -1 the positive integer -c_m-1 at least doubles and is bounded by C-1. Neither case can have even one edge if C<=1. For c_m=0 or -1 a period-preserving choice (k,t)=(bh,ah) works indefinitely, using respectively 0 or B^t-1 as the digit block. Periodicity gives the stated density. The phase sequence 1,2,...,2^L realizes L consecutive edges with A=B=2, including the zero-edge case. The independent-root citation is mathematically applicable: (E-A)(E^h-1) annihilates the recurrence and A is the unique simple dominant root. The inspected source is an arXiv preprint; a separate publication status is not established. Read the frozen proof, verification note and code without executing the upload. A bounded independent integer replay checked 1,152 candidates (58 admissible), 59,536 signed floor cases and sharp examples through L=12; it is not an unbounded proof.
